drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 70-year-old male admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.67, creatinine 1.91-1.94, hemoglobin 14.8-14.9, platelets 228-230, sodium 140, wbc 8.5-8.7; vitals dbp 72-76, heart_rate 83-87, map 87-90, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 115-121, spo2 97-98, temp 36.9-37.1
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Chronic kidney disease stage 3. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.93-1.95, hemoglobin 14.7, platelets 222-226, sodium 140-141, wbc 8.7-8.8; vitals dbp 74-77, heart_rate 82-87, map 89-92, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 115-122, spo2 97-98, temp 36.9-37.1
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Chronic kidney disease stage 3. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 70-year-old male, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Chronic kidney disease stage 3. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
